# 03-angular-client: Upgrade Angular client to latest stable

Update the Angular 21 client in HamEvent/ClientApp to the verified latest stable Angular 22.2.3, including compatible Angular Material/CDK, CLI, build tools, TypeScript and runtime packages and lockfile. Review obsolete Angular flex-layout and other dependencies; use Angular migrations where available, preserving existing UI and tests. The local Node.js 26 runtime meets Angular 22's reported engine range.

**Done when**: The client installs with a consistent lockfile, builds, and its runnable tests and i18n checks pass without upgrade-related errors; any unsupported third-party dependencies are recorded.

## Research Findings
- `HamEvent/ClientApp/package.json` and package-lock.json currently pin Angular 21 ranges, devkit/CLI/compiler-cli 21 and TypeScript ~5.9.3. Baseline `npm run build` succeeds; node_modules and package-lock.json exist.
- Public npm reports @angular/core/compiler 22.2.3, @angular/material/CDK, CLI and build-angular 22.2.4. Compiler-cli requires TypeScript >=6.0 <6.1; 6.0.3 is available. Angular core accepts zone.js ~0.15 or ~0.16; keep current 0.15 unless incompatibility requires change. Existing Node.js 26.5.1 satisfies Angular's engine requirement.
- The classic browser + Karma builders and NgModules are present in angular.json; upgrade compatible packages without redesigning builders or changing the application architecture. Existing @angular/flex-layout 15 beta (last published 2023) has peer `@angular/core >=15.0.2`, so peer resolution permits Angular 22, but it is obsolete and its usage across templates/components should be listed as a deferred modernization recommendation unless migration is required to build.
- Client uses Material and BrowserAnimationsModule. `src/themes.scss` contains old Material theming syntax but is not referenced from angular.json styles, so do not change unused legacy file for this upgrade. Peer dependencies of ngx-pagination and @ngx-translate/core allow Angular 22.
- Scope is the Angular dependency set and migrations, one related application; leave unrelated npm libraries for the final recommendations audit. Run installation using the public registry and `--userconfig=NUL` due to Azure feed E401; keep the lockfile consistent. No mandatory decomposition hint applies.
- Resumed installation: initial npm install failed ERESOLVE because node_modules contained Angular 21 with TypeScript 5.9; a one-time lockfile-only regeneration was required to leave the stale peer graph, and `npm ci` subsequently succeeded without force after retrying a transient network ECONNRESET. npm reports 24 advisories at this point; audit before completion. `glob@10.5.0` is pulled by Jest 30.2.0's @jest/reporters, jest-config and jest-runtime; Jest 30.5.2 uses glob ^13.0.6. Upgrade Jest within major 30 to resolve this deprecated transitive version rather than overriding glob globally. Other deprecations (Angular Webpack builder, animations, flex-layout) need later migration review.
- Further repo-wide search found no Jest scripts, configuration or test imports (only its package.json entry). Registry timeouts and a missing offline @jest/core packument block a trustworthy Jest 30.5.2 installation, so remove this unused development dependency instead of keeping an inconsistent manifest and lockfile; Karma and Playwright remain the actual test runners. Confirm a clean `npm ci` and absence of glob@10.5.0 after lockfile regeneration. Do not introduce global glob overrides or force vulnerable dependency versions.
- Current checkpoint: Angular 22.2.x / Material and CLI 22.2.x, TypeScript 6.0.3 and an updated lockfile compile; nine-locale parity, 72 ChromeHeadless tests and the production build pass locally. The build warns that the initial bundle exceeds its 1.20 MB budget by 702 bytes and the Webpack browser builder is deprecated; assess both in integration validation rather than hiding the warning.
- CI is being aligned with Node 24 and .NET 10. Before a TEST deployment, confirm the .NET 10 Hosting Bundle on IIS and set the TEST environment variable `DOTNET10_HOSTING_READY=true` only after confirmation. Deployment requires an archived TEST database backup and preserves `App_Data/QSOs.db`. The retired legacy build workflow must not be used for deployment. PROD deployment remains manual and should be reviewed separately before use.
